source: GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit), Support of Regional Economic Cooperation in Asia (SRECA), in cooperation with MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture — គោលការណ៍ណែនាំអំពីការនាំចេញផ្លែស្វាយស្រស់ពីប្រទេសកម្ពុជាទៅប្រទេសចិន (Guideline on Fresh Mango Export from Cambodia to China), Final Version, Phnom Penh, December 2020, 67pp
text:
Overview of China's import-control system for fresh mango, per the GIZ/SRECA guideline (December 2020 edition).

Since 2018, China's General Administration of Customs (GACC) absorbed the plant/animal quarantine functions previously handled by AQSIQ (the Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine), following a State Council reorganization. GACC is now the single authority responsible for both customs and phytosanitary/quarantine control for agricultural imports, including fresh mango from Cambodia.

Fresh mango exports to China are governed by a bilateral phytosanitary protocol between Cambodia's MAFF and China's GACC. Only orchards and packing houses that have been registered and approved under this protocol may supply fruit for export; GACC publishes a public list of approved exporting countries and facilities.

Registered exporters and orchards gain rights including: legal standing to export; official recognition of their orchard/product as meeting the agreed quality standard; the right to fast, compliant customs clearance; and legal protection of their registered trademark or origin claim. In exchange, registered parties take on obligations including: not altering registered orchard details without notifying the authority; reporting production and harvest volumes and any changes; maintaining full traceability and quality control so origin is never mixed or misrepresented; and accepting legal responsibility for any violation of the registration or quarantine terms.

GACC's inspection structure runs from the national level (GACC headquarters, Animal and Plant Quarantine Division) down to provincial customs districts (e.g., Nanning Customs District in Guangxi) and city/port-level local customs offices with inspection sections. Cambodian mango destined for southern China commonly moves through checkpoints in the Guangxi region, including Pingxiang (bordering Vietnam) and Qinzhou, as well as major markets/ports in Guangzhou (Huangpu), Shenzhen, and Shantou.
